chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Overview.
description: Create images from a text prompt or transform your own pictures. Pick a model, aspect ratio and quality in the prompt bar, click Generate, and your images appear in a gallery above it.
shortDescription: Create images from a text prompt or transform your own pictures. Pick a model, aspect ratio and quality in the prompt bar, click Generate, and your images appear in a gallery above it.
fullDescription: Image Studio has a gallery on top and a prompt bar at the bottom. There is no separate text-to-image / image-to-image switch: the studio works in text-to-image mode until you add a reference image, and then switches to an image-to-image version of the same model when one exists. In the prompt bar you can add reference images, type a prompt, open the Model picker (tabs All, Text to Image, Image to Image, provider icons and a search box), set the aspect ratio, resolution (when the model has it), model-specific parameters, an Effect Type (for models that have effects), and a batch size of 1 to 4. A Draw button opens Draw to Edit, Recipes opens the prompt-recipe hub, and the Library button (or Saved) lets you reuse earlier uploads and generations.
bestFor: Creators who need images quickly with many model choices.
whenToUse:
- New images from text
- Restyling or transforming your pictures
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Edit Studio for single-purpose tools (upscale, cut-out)

chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Overview.
- Use Layers Studio for layers, expansion and color grading
- Use Video Studio for video
businessValue: Fast visual content from a single prompt bar.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). How to use.
howToUse: Open Image Studio from the studio tab bar (tab 'Image Studio') or go to /studio/image. Click the model button in the prompt bar (it shows the current model name) to open the Model list. Use the tabs All, Text to Image or Image to Image, the provider icons (or All Providers) and the Search models... box, then click a model. Type what you want in the prompt box: 'Describe the image you want to create'.
howToSteps:
- Open Image Studio from the studio tab bar (tab 'Image Studio') or go to /studio/image.
- Click the model button in the prompt bar (it shows the current model name) to open the Model list. Use the tabs All, Text to Image or Image to Image, the provider icons (or All Providers) and the Search models... box, then click a model.
- Type what you want in the prompt box: 'Describe the image you want to create'.
- Optional, to transform your own picture: click the reference-image button (tooltip 'Reference image' or 'Add up to N images'), click 'Upload new' (or 'Upload files' when several are allowed), choose image files (max 10MB each) and, for multi-image models, click Done. You can also drag image files onto the studio, or choose a saved image with Library. The prompt placeholder changes to 'Describe how to transform this image (optional)'.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). How to use.
- Click the aspect-ratio button and choose a ratio. If a quality/resolution button is shown, click it and choose a resolution.
- Optional: open PARAMS (if shown) for extra settings of the chosen model, open Effect Type (if shown for an image-to-image model), and use the - and + buttons to set how many images to create (1 to 4).
- Click Generate. The button shows 'Generating...' until the images arrive.
- Your images appear in the gallery. Click one to open a fullscreen preview; hover it to Download or Delete (confirm prompt), copy the prompt, or publish.
- To go on from a result, add it again as a reference image (Upload new or Library) and generate again.
gettingStarted:
- Open Image Studio (/studio/image).
- Type a prompt in the prompt bar.
- Check the model, aspect ratio and (if shown) resolution buttons.
- Click Generate.
- Click an image in the gallery to preview it; hover it and use Download to save it.
tips:
- Add a reference image to move from text-to-image to image-to-image: the studio switches to the model's image-reference version automatically; if the model cannot take references you see '<model> does not support image references.'
- Describe subject, style, lighting and composition in the prompt for more predictable results.
- Use batch size 2 to 4 to get several options at once.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). How to use.
- The studio remembers your prompt, model, settings and gallery in this browser between visits (stored locally).
- Use Library to reuse files you uploaded or generated in other studios.
bestPractices:
- Choose the model first, then the aspect ratio, because available ratios and resolutions depend on the model.
- For image-to-image, wait for the reference thumbnail to appear before clicking Generate.
- Use clear reference images under 10MB.
- Download the images you want to keep; the gallery is stored in your browser (the last 50 images).

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Features.
keyFeatures:
- Prompt bar with Model picker (tabs All, Text to Image, Image to Image; provider filter; Search models...)
- Reference images: add them with the reference button, drag files onto the studio, or pick from Library; the number allowed depends on the model
- Aspect ratio, resolution (shown only for models that have it), model-specific PARAMS, and Effect Type (models with effects)
- Batch size stepper from 1 to 4 images per click (shown as n/4)
- Swap Face upload for face-swap models
- Draw to Edit modal (Draw button) for sketching on an image and generating from it
- Gallery with Download, Delete, copy, publish and fullscreen preview

- feature: Reference images | explanation: Guide the result with your pictures. | whyToUse: Keep a subject or composition | inputRequired: Image files | restrictions: 10MB each; count depends on the model
- feature: Gallery actions | explanation: Hover a tile for copy, publish, Download and Delete; click for fullscreen. | whyToUse: Review and save results | inputRequired: None | restrictions: Delete asks for confirmation
advancedFeatures:
- Multiple reference images
- Effect Type
- PARAMS model settings
- Draw to Edit
- Batch size up to 4
- Recipes and Library

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Problems and limits.
troubleshooting:
- Nothing is generated: Read the message shown, e.g. 'Please enter a prompt to generate an image.' or 'Please upload a reference image first.'
- '<model> does not support image references.': Click the model button and choose a model from the Image to Image tab.
- Reference upload fails: Check the file is an image under 10MB.
- Image generation failed: Try another model or a simpler prompt.
troubleshootingSteps:
- issue: Nothing is generated | steps:; - Read the message shown, e.g. 'Please enter a prompt to generate an image.' or 'Please upload a reference image first.'; - Fix it and click Generate again.; - If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
- issue: '<model> does not support image references.' | steps:; - Click the model button and choose a model from the Image to Image tab.
- issue: Reference upload fails | steps:; - Check the file is an image under 10MB.; - Try again or use Library.
- issue: Image generation failed | steps:; - Try another model or a simpler prompt.; - Check your key and balance.
commonProblems:
- problem: I can't find an image-to-image switch | whyItHappens: Mode follows whether reference images are present | howToFix: Add a reference image with the reference button
- problem: Resolution button missing | whyItHappens: The selected model has no resolution options | howToFix: Choose another model

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Problems and limits.
limitations:
- Generation needs your own MuAPI key
- Reference images: max 10MB per file; count and aspect ratios depend on the model
- Gallery history kept in this browser: last 50 images
- There is no seed, strength slider or inpainting control in this screen
limitationDetails:
- limitation: MuAPI key required | impact: Generate fails | workaround: Open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key
- limitation: 10MB per reference image | impact: Larger files are rejected with an alert | workaround: Resize or compress
- limitation: Browser-stored history | impact: History may not follow you to another browser | workaround: Download images you need
faqs:
- question: How do I do image-to-image? | answer: Add a reference image with the reference button, drag a file in, or use Library. There is no separate switch.
- question: How big can reference images be? | answer: Up to 10MB per image.
- question: How many reference images? | answer: It depends on the model; the button tooltip says 'Add up to N images'.
- question: How many images per click? | answer: 1 to 4, set with the - and + stepper.
- question: Does it have a seed or strength slider? | answer: No. Extra settings, if any, appear under PARAMS for the chosen model.
- question: Where are my images saved? | answer: In the gallery in this browser (last 50). Click Download to keep a file.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Image Studio (/studio/image). Problems and limits.
- question: What is Draw? | answer: Draw to Edit: sketch on a canvas and generate from it with Nano Banana 2 or Nano Banana Pro.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). Overview.
description: Create AI video from a prompt, a still image, start and end frames, references or an existing video. Choose a model, then a video mode, duration, aspect ratio and resolution in the prompt bar and click Generate.
shortDescription: Create AI video from a prompt, a still image, start and end frames, references or an existing video. Choose a model, then a video mode, duration, aspect ratio and resolution in the prompt bar and click Generate.
fullDescription: Video Studio has a gallery of your videos on top and a prompt bar at the bottom. In the prompt bar you add reference media (images, videos, audio, depending on the model), type a prompt, open the Model picker (tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video, Video Tools), and then use the controls that the selected model provides: a video-mode button (From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video, Transfer motion), a Speed button (some models), a Settings button (Quality and a Generation service choice under Advanced, plus model options such as Seed or Generate audio), Aspect Ratio, Duration, Resolution, and Effect. Only the controls that apply to the chosen model and mode are shown. A Draw button lets you sketch a reference image. Seedance and Veo have extra video tools in the Model picker (continue a result, remove watermark, create a 4K copy).

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). Overview.
bestFor: Creators making short AI video.
whenToUse:
- New AI video from text, images or video
- Animating stills, transferring motion, editing or extending clips
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Edit Studio for single-purpose tools such as Watermark Remover or Face Swap cards
- Use Image Studio for stills
- Use Lip Sync for talking footage
businessValue: Fast video content from prompts and images.

chunks.title: Video Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). How to use.
howToUse: Open Video Studio from the studio tab bar (tab 'Video Studio') or go to /studio/video. Click the model button in the prompt bar. In the Model list use the tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video or Video Tools, the provider icons (or All Providers) and the Search models... box, then click a model. If a video-mode button appears next to the model button, click it (header 'Video mode') and choose what you want to do: From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video or Transfer motion. Each item has a one-line description.
howToSteps:
- Open Video Studio from the studio tab bar (tab 'Video Studio') or go to /studio/video.
- Click the model button in the prompt bar. In the Model list use the tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video or Video Tools, the provider icons (or All Providers) and the Search models... box, then click a model.
- If a video-mode button appears next to the model button, click it (header 'Video mode') and choose what you want to do: From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video or Transfer motion. Each item has a one-line description.

chunks.title: Video Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). How to use.
- Add the media the mode needs using the upload buttons in the prompt bar (hover for tooltips such as 'Upload start frame', 'Upload end frame', 'Upload up to N reference images', 'Upload up to N reference videos'). Images must be under 10MB; videos and audio under 50MB. You can also pick saved files with Library.
- Type your prompt. The placeholder tells you what to write: for example 'Describe the video you want to create', 'Describe how to edit the video', or 'Describe the motion (optional)'.
- Set the options that are shown: Speed (if shown), Settings (Quality, Generation service under Advanced, and model options), Aspect Ratio, Effect, Duration and Resolution. Buttons that do not apply to the model are not shown.
- Click Generate. The button shows 'Generating...' and is disabled until the video returns (or while an upload is running).
- Your video appears at the top of the gallery. Hover a tile to play it, click to open the fullscreen player; use the hover buttons to Download or Delete it (Delete asks to confirm).
- To continue a Seedance 2.0 video, hover its tile and click Extend, then describe how to continue and click Generate.
gettingStarted:
- Open Video Studio (/studio/video).
- Pick a model with the model button.
- Type a prompt (or upload an image to animate it).
- Check Aspect Ratio, Duration and Resolution if shown.

chunks.title: Video Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). How to use.
- Click Generate and wait for the video in the gallery.
tips:
- Start with 'From prompt' for text-to-video, and 'Animate image' to bring a still to life.
- Use 'Start & end frames' to control the first and last picture (upload start frame, then end frame).
- Use 'Use references' to guide a video with uploaded images, videos or audio on models that accept them.
- If you upload a file the current model cannot use, the studio switches to a version of the same family that can, or tells you '<family> does not support <image/video/audio> references.'
- Duration, resolution and aspect ratio choices differ by model; if a choice is greyed out the message 'Unavailable for this version' appears.
- Prompt, model and gallery are remembered in this browser.
bestPractices:
- Choose the model and mode first; the other controls depend on them.
- Wait for uploads to finish before clicking Generate.
- Describe subject, action, setting and camera in one or two sentences.
- Download videos you want to keep; the gallery is stored in your browser.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). Features.
keyFeatures:
- Model picker with tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video, Video Tools, provider icons and Search models...
- Video-mode menu per model family: From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video, Transfer motion
- Reference uploads for images (10MB each), videos (50MB each) and audio (50MB each) where the model accepts them; drag-and-drop works on the upload buttons and on the whole studio
- Per-model Settings: Quality, Generation service (Standard, Pro, Fast and so on) and options such as Seed, Generate audio
- Seedance video tools (Continue a Seedance 2.0 result, Remove watermark) and Veo video tools (Continue Veo 3.1, Create a 4K copy) inside the Model picker
- Extend button on Seedance 2.0 results in the gallery
- Gallery with hover actions (Download, Delete, copy, publish) and fullscreen preview

- feature: Text to video | explanation: Prompt-only generation. | whyToUse: New clips | inputRequired: Prompt | restrictions: Model-dependent
- feature: Image to video | explanation: Animate a still. | whyToUse: Bring pictures to life | inputRequired: Image | restrictions: 10MB images
- feature: Video tools | explanation: Edit, extend, motion transfer, watermark removal and similar tools. | whyToUse: Work with existing video | inputRequired: Video | restrictions: 50MB videos
advancedFeatures:
- Video modes

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Video Studio (/studio/video). Problems and limits.
troubleshooting:
- A message appears when I click Generate: Read it: it names the missing item, for example 'Please upload a video first.' or 'Please upload a reference image for motion control.'
- Upload rejected or failed: Check size (image 10MB, video/audio 50MB) and file type.
- 'Choose a compatible <family> result to continue.': Generate a video with that family first, or click Extend on a Seedance 2.0 result in the gallery.
- No video URL returned by API: Try again, or choose another model or settings.
troubleshootingSteps:
- issue: A message appears when I click Generate | steps:; - Read it: it names the missing item, for example 'Please upload a video first.' or 'Please upload a reference image for motion control.'; - Add it and click Generate again.; - If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
- issue: Upload rejected or failed | steps:; - Check size (image 10MB, video/audio 50MB) and file type.; - Wait for the current upload to finish ('Wait for the current upload to finish, then add these files again.').
- issue: 'Choose a compatible <family> result to continue.' | steps:; - Generate a video with that family first, or click Extend on a Seedance 2.0 result in the gallery.
- issue: No video URL returned by API | steps:; - Try again, or choose another model or settings.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Overview.
description: Generate music, speech, voice clones and sound with a model picker that covers Suno, Minimax, ElevenLabs, Gemini TTS, Fish Audio, Lyria and MMAudio models, with a built-in audio player and a generation history.
shortDescription: Pick an audio model, fill in the settings that model asks for, click Generate Track, then play and save the result in the built-in player.
fullDescription: Audio Studio has one settings panel on the left and a player area on the right. The panel is built from the model you choose: the Audio Model dropdown lists many music, speech, voice-cloning and sound models, and the fields below it (prompt, style, toggles, sliders, dropdowns, audio upload boxes) change to match the selected model. An Estimated cost line sits above the Generate Track button. When a track is ready it appears in a player with Play/Pause, a seek bar, volume and a Save button, and the last results are kept in a Generation History strip at the bottom of the page.
bestFor: Creators who need music, narration or sound clips from a model picker with a built-in player.
whenToUse:
- You need music, a voiceover, a cloned voice or a sound clip
- You want to remix, extend or add vocals to your own audio
- You want a quick preview player and mp3 download
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Lip Sync Studio when you want a face to speak or sing to your audio

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Overview.
- Use Video Studio when you want moving pictures
- Use Vibe Motion for animated motion graphics
businessValue: Produces usable audio inside the same workspace as the visual studios, so music and voice can be made without separate tools.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). How to use.
howToUse: Open Audio Studio, choose a model under Audio Model, fill in the fields that appear for that model (for the default Suno Create Music model: Style is required), check Estimated cost, click Generate Track, then play the result and click Save to download it.
howToSteps:
- Open the Audio Studio tab (route /studio/audio). The settings panel is on the left and the player area on the right.
- Under Audio Model, click the dropdown (it shows Suno Create Music at first) and pick the model you want. Each entry shows a one-line description; the chosen model's description also appears under Description.
- Fill in the fields shown for that model. Fields marked as required by the model must be completed or you get the message 'Please complete the required field: <field name>'. For Suno Create Music only Style is required; for Minimax Speech HD / Turbo the Prompt and Voice ID are required; for MiniMax Music 3.0 both Prompt and Lyrics are required.
- If the model has an upload box (for example Audio URL, Instrumental Audio, Vocal Audio, Voice Sample URL, Mashup Tracks), click the box labelled 'Upload audio track' or drag an audio file onto it. When the upload finishes the box shows the file name and 'Ready to generate'. Click Clear to remove the file.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). How to use.
- Optional: use the toggles, sliders and dropdowns (for example Custom Mode, Instrumental, Vocal Gender, Style Weight, Speed, Emotion) to fine-tune the result. For Suno models, turn Instrumental off if you want your Prompt sung as lyrics.
- Look at Estimated cost above the button to see the price estimate (it shows 'calculating…' while it updates, or a dash if no estimate is available).
- Click Generate Track. The button changes to 'Generating Audio...' and the right side shows 'Generating Soundtrack'. Wait until the player appears.
- Under 'Now Playing', press the round Play button to listen, click the bar to jump to a point, use the speaker button (Mute/Unmute) and the volume slider that appears when you hover it.
- Click Save to download the audio (mp3 file named after the track title, or generated_audio.mp3).
- To try again, click New Generation: your settings stay in place so you can adjust them. Earlier results are listed under 'Generation History' at the bottom; click a card to play it again.
gettingStarted:
- Open Audio Studio from the studio tabs (route /studio/audio).
- Leave Audio Model on Suno Create Music for your first song.
- In Style type a genre such as Jazz, Classical, Electronic, Pop, Rock or Hip-hop (this field is required).

chunks.title: Audio Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). How to use.
- Turn Instrumental off if you want vocals, and type lyrics into Prompt (with Instrumental on, no lyrics are sung); optionally type a Title.
- Click Generate Track and wait for the player.
- Press Play under 'Now Playing', then click Save to download.
tips:
- Suno's Prompt field is described as the exact lyrics that will be sung; describe the sound in Style and put lyrics only in Prompt.
- Suno Create Music starts with Instrumental switched on; switch it off when you want sung lyrics.
- Use Negative Tags (for example 'Heavy Metal, Upbeat Drums') to steer Suno away from styles you do not want.
- Watch Estimated cost before clicking Generate Track, especially after changing sliders or toggles.
- Click a Generation History card to replay earlier results without regenerating.
- For Suno Remix Music and Suno Extend Music the model description says the uploaded audio should not exceed 2 minutes.
bestPractices:
- Pick the model by task: Suno models for songs, Minimax Speech / ElevenLabs / Gemini / Fish models for spoken voice, MM Audio V2 or Suno Generate Sounds for effects and loops, Lyria for short clips.
- Fill in the required fields first; the studio stops with a message if one is empty.
- Keep voice or source samples clean and short; the Suno Voice Cloning description asks for a clean 10-second recording.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). How to use.
- Use New Generation to iterate: your last settings are kept so you only change what you want to improve.
- Name your track in Title (when the model has it) so the downloaded file and history card are easy to recognise.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Problems and limits.
troubleshooting:
- If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
- 'Please complete the required field' means a required box is empty.
- 'Audio file exceeds 20MB limit.' or 'Invalid file type' means the upload was refused; use an mp3 or wav under 10 MB.
- 'Audio generation failed' or an error toast means the request failed; check your balance and try again.
- No sung vocals on a Suno track: switch Instrumental off and put lyrics in Prompt.
troubleshootingSteps:
- issue: Generation is blocked or fails immediately | steps:; - If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.; - Read the red toast in the top-right corner for the error text.; - Click Generate Track again.
- issue: Message 'Please complete the required field' | steps:; - Note the field name in the message.; - Fill that field (Style for Suno Create Music, Prompt and Voice ID for Minimax Speech, an uploaded audio for remix / extend / voice-clone models).; - Click Generate Track again.
- issue: Upload refused or alert shown | steps:; - Check the file is mp3 or wav (webm also accepted) and under 10 MB.; - Click Clear if an old file is attached, then upload again.; - Wait for 'Ready to generate' before generating.
- issue: Suno track has no vocals | steps:; - Turn Instrumental off.; - Type your lyrics in Prompt.; - Click Generate Track.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Problems and limits.
- issue: Result does not play | steps:; - Press Play again; the player reloads when the track changes.; - Click Save to download the file and play it locally.; - Generate again if the track still fails.
commonProblems:
- problem: Track is instrumental but I wanted a singer | whyItHappens: Instrumental is on by default for Suno Create Music. | howToFix: Turn Instrumental off and enter lyrics in Prompt.
- problem: Cannot pick Suno V4 or V5.5 | whyItHappens: The model-version dropdown is hidden in this studio and V5 is the default. | howToFix: Use the default; there is no version picker in the form.
- problem: m4a file will not upload | whyItHappens: Only mp3, wav and webm audio pass the upload check, despite the on-screen hint. | howToFix: Convert to mp3 or wav under 10 MB.
- problem: Alert says 20MB but my 15 MB file was refused | whyItHappens: The message text and the enforced limit differ; the enforced audio limit is 10 MB. | howToFix: Compress or trim the audio below 10 MB.
limitations:
- Generation needs your MuAPI key and available balance.
- Each model has its own required fields; the studio blocks generation until they are filled.
- The studio waits for a result by checking every 2 seconds for up to 900 checks (about 30 minutes) before giving up.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Problems and limits.
- Uploaded audio is limited to 10 MB and to mp3, wav or webm files by the upload contract, even though the upload box hint says 'MP3, WAV, M4A up to 20MB'.
- The Suno model-version dropdown is not shown; Suno runs on its default version (V5).
- Models whose inputs are lists (ElevenLabs Text to Dialogue V3 'Dialogue Script', Gemini TTS 'Speakers' and 'Dialogue Turns') are displayed as plain text boxes.
limitationDetails:
- limitation: Audio upload size and type | impact: Files over 10 MB are rejected (the alert text still says 20MB); m4a files are refused with 'Invalid file type'. | workaround: Export the file as mp3 or wav under 10 MB and upload again.
- limitation: Required fields | impact: Clicking Generate Track with an empty required field shows 'Please complete the required field: <field>'. | workaround: Fill the named field (for Suno Create Music that is Style).
- limitation: Suno version selection | impact: You cannot choose V3.5 to V5.5 from the form; the default V5 is used. | workaround: None in the studio form.
- limitation: List-style inputs | impact: Dialogue Script, Speakers and Dialogue Turns appear as simple text boxes, so the expected structure is not guided. | workaround: Use the single-prompt speech models (Minimax Speech, ElevenLabs TTS Turbo 2.5, Eleven v4, Fish Audio S2.1 Pro) if you only need plain narration.
faqs:

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Problems and limits.
- question: Where do I open Audio Studio? | answer: From the Audio Studio tab, route /studio/audio.
- question: Which model should I start with? | answer: The Audio Model dropdown starts on Suno Create Music, which only requires Style. For spoken audio choose a speech model such as Minimax Speech HD.
- question: How do I get lyrics sung? | answer: Turn Instrumental off and type the lyrics in Prompt. The model hint says the prompt is used as the exact lyrics.
- question: Can I choose the Suno version? | answer: Not in this studio form: the Model field is hidden and V5 is the default.
- question: What audio files can I upload? | answer: Audio files through the upload boxes; the upload contract accepts mp3 (audio/mpeg), wav and webm audio up to 10 MB. The box hint mentions M4A and 20MB but the code does not accept m4a or more than 10 MB.
- question: How do I download the result? | answer: Click Save in the player. It saves an .mp3 named after your Title (or generated_audio.mp3).
- question: Where are my previous results? | answer: In the Generation History grid at the bottom of the page; click a card to play it. It keeps up to 30 items in your browser.
- question: Does it show what a generation will cost? | answer: Yes, an Estimated cost line above Generate Track, shown as 'calculating…' while updating or a dash if unavailable.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits

Audio Studio (/studio/audio). Problems and limits.
- question: What does New Generation do? | answer: It returns to the settings view and keeps your parameters so you can adjust them.
- question: Generation is blocked, what do I check? | answer: Open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Overview
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Overview.
description: Upload a long video (or paste a link to one), choose an aspect ratio and how many highlights you want, and get back short highlight clips, or only timing coordinates if you switch on Coordinates Only.
shortDescription: Upload a long video (or paste a link to one), choose an aspect ratio and how many highlights you want, and get back short highlight clips, or only timing coordinates if you switch on Coordinates Only.
fullDescription: AI Clipping takes one source video and sends it, with your chosen aspect ratio, highlight count and the Coordinates Only setting, to the MuAPI ai-clipping service. In the default mode the result is a gallery of rendered highlight clips (Clips Gallery Mode) that you can preview, copy a link to, download or post. With Coordinates Only switched on you instead get a Highlights Timeline next to the original video player (Timeline Seek Mode), where each highlight shows a start and end time and clicking it jumps the player to that moment. Each run is kept in a Clipping History Runs list in your browser. The text box at the bottom of the studio accepts a pasted video link, and its text is not sent to the clipping service.
bestFor: Creators, social media managers and marketers who repurpose long recordings into short clips.
whenToUse:
- You have a long recording and want short highlight clips

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Overview
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Overview.
- You only need start and end times of highlight moments
- You want several aspect ratios of the same source video by running it more than once
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Video Studio to generate new video from text or images
- Use the social publishing modal (the post button on a clip) when you are ready to publish a clip
- Use Lip Sync or Recast studios to change what is said or who appears in a video
businessValue: AI Clipping reduces the time spent scrubbing through long videos by returning highlight clips or highlight times from one request. You choose the output shape and how many highlights to ask for, and everything is reviewed in the same screen.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — How to use
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). How to use.
howToUse: Open AI Clipping at /studio/clipping, add a source video (upload, drag and drop, pick from Saved, or paste a direct video link into the text box), choose the aspect ratio and the Max Highlights count, optionally switch on Coordinates Only, then click Generate. Clips appear under Extracted Video Clips; in Coordinates Only mode a Highlights Timeline appears instead.
howToSteps:
- Open AI Clipping: choose AI Clipping in the studio list, or go to /studio/clipping.
- Add your source video using any one of these: click the video-camera upload button at the left of the bottom bar (tooltip Upload source video) and choose a video file of up to 100 MB; drag a video file onto that button; click Saved and choose a video under Videos in Your library; or paste a link that starts with http:// or https:// into the text box (it moves into the source slot automatically).
- Check that a small video preview appears in the bottom bar. Use its x button (tooltip Clear video) if you chose the wrong video.
- Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 9:16 at first) and pick one of 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3 or 3:4 from the Aspect Ratio menu.
- Click the highlights button (it shows 3 Highlights at first). In the Max Highlights menu drag the Limit: slider between 1 and 60.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — How to use
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). How to use.
- Optional: click Coordinates Only if you want only timing data and not rendered clips. It is off by default; the button is highlighted when on.
- Click Generate. The button changes to Generating... until the service finishes; long videos can take a while.
- When it finishes you see either Extracted Video Clips (default) or, with Coordinates Only, the Original Video Player and Highlights Timeline. Hover a clip to preview it, use Copy Link or Download on the hover buttons, or click a timeline entry (Seek & Play) to jump the player to that highlight.
- Click Back to History to leave the result. Earlier runs appear under Clipping History Runs; click a card to reopen it.
gettingStarted:
- Open AI Clipping from the studio list (/studio/clipping).
- Add a video with the Upload source video button, drag and drop, Saved, or by pasting an http:// or https:// video link into the text box.
- Leave the aspect ratio at 9:16 and the Max Highlights at 3 for a first test, or change them from the two buttons in the bottom bar.
- Click Generate and wait while the button shows Generating...
- Review the Extracted Video Clips, then use Copy Link or Download on the clips you want to keep.
- Try Coordinates Only next to see the Highlights Timeline.
tips:
- Try a first run with the default 3 highlights, then increase the Max Highlights slider if you need more.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — How to use
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). How to use.
- Pick the aspect ratio before you click Generate; it is sent with the request.
- Keep uploads under 100 MB; for bigger files trim or compress the video first.
- Use Coordinates Only to review where highlights fall before spending time on clip files.
- Your history stays in this browser only, so download clips you want to keep.
bestPractices:
- Start with a short test video to confirm the settings, then run the full-length one.
- Choose the aspect ratio that matches where you will post: 9:16 for vertical feeds, 16:9 for wide, 1:1 or 4:5 for feed posts.
- Ask for a few more highlights than you need and pick the best in review.
- Download or copy the link of each clip you plan to use right after the run.
- If you paste a link, use a direct link to a video file rather than a web page.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Features
chunks.text:

keyFeatures:

featureExplanations:
- feature: Source video upload and library | explanation: Upload a video file, drag one onto the upload button, or choose a previous upload or generated video under Saved (a Your library panel with Loading and an empty message when nothing is saved). | whyToUse: Reuse videos you already added in any studio without uploading again. | inputRequired: video file or saved video | restrictions: 100 MB maximum per uploaded file.
- feature: Aspect ratio | explanation: Sets the aspect ratio sent with the request; the clip cards in the gallery are shown in that shape. | whyToUse: Match the clips to TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube or square feeds. | inputRequired: none (default 9:16) | restrictions: Six options only.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Features

AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Features.

- feature: Coordinates Only | explanation: Returns timing coordinates (start, end, optional label and score) and shows them as a Highlights Timeline beside the Original Video Player. | whyToUse: Plan your own edits without rendered clips. | inputRequired: source video | restrictions: No clip files in this mode, so there is nothing to download from the timeline.
- feature: Clipping History Runs | explanation: Past runs are listed as cards (up to 30) with the source file name, mode label and aspect ratio. Click a card to reopen it; hover a card and use the trash button (Delete from history) to remove it. | whyToUse: Come back to earlier results without re-running. | inputRequired: none | restrictions: Stored in this browser only (local storage), so it is not shared across browsers or devices.

advancedFeatureExplanations:

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Features
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Features.
- feature: Saved library | explanation: Saved opens Your library with Videos so you can reuse an earlier upload or generated video as the source. | useCase: Re-clipping a video with different settings | restrictions: Only shown while no source video is set

- Clips Gallery Mode

modeExplanations:
- mode: Clips Gallery Mode | description: Default. After Generate, the main area shows the heading Extracted Video Clips and a grid of rendered clips labelled Clip #1, Clip #2 and so on. Clips preview silently when you hover over them. | acronymExpanded: N/A | useCase: Getting finished short clips to download or post
- mode: Timeline Seek Mode | description: Used when Coordinates Only is on. The main area shows the Original Video Player and a Highlights Timeline list. Each entry shows its start and end time, duration, and a score if one is returned; clicking it seeks the player to the start and plays (Seek & Play). | acronymExpanded: N/A | useCase: Finding highlight moments or copying times into another editing tool
modelCapabilities: The studio uses a single backend service, ai-clipping, with no model selector. It receives the video URL, the number of highlights, the aspect ratio and the coordinates-only flag.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Features
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Features.
modelExplanations: There is no model picker in AI Clipping. The label AI Clipping in the bottom bar only identifies the service. The settings sent are the video URL, the Max Highlights number, the aspect ratio and whether Coordinates Only is on. The results page lists whatever the service returns, so the number of clips can differ from the number you requested.

Add it with the video upload button (tooltip Upload source video), by dragging a video file onto that button, by choosing a video under Saved, or by pasting a link that starts with http:// or https:// into the bottom text box. Once added, a small preview with a x button (tooltip Clear video) replaces the upload button. | required: true | whenToUse: Always: Generate shows an alert asking you to upload a video or paste a video URL if none is set. | restrictions: Uploaded files over 100 MB are rejected before upload. Only files the browser reports as video are accepted. A pasted link is used as-is, so it should be a direct link to a video file that the clipping service can fetch.

The button shows the current value (default 9:16); the menu titled Aspect Ratio lists 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3 and 3:4. | required: false | whenToUse: Pick the shape of the platform you will post to before generating. | restrictions: Only the six listed ratios are offered.

A value that is only a link starting with http:// or https:// is moved into the source video slot and the box is cleared. | required: false | whenToUse: Mainly as a quick place to paste a video link. | restrictions: Other text typed here is not included in the clipping request (the request carries only the video URL, highlight count, aspect ratio and the coordinates flag).

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Problems and limits.
troubleshooting:
- Generate does nothing except show an alert
- Upload failed or file too large
- Generation failed
- No clips or highlights in the result
troubleshootingSteps:
- issue: Generate does nothing except show an alert | steps:; - Check that a video preview is visible in the bottom bar.; - If not, upload a video, choose one under Saved, or paste a direct video link.; - Click Generate again.
- issue: Upload failed or file too large | steps:; - Check the file is a video and under 100 MB.; - Trim or compress it, then upload again.; - Or paste a link to a hosted copy of the video into the text box.
- issue: Generation failed | steps:; - Read the red error message in the bottom-right corner (it stays about 7 seconds).; - If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.; - Try again with a smaller or shorter video, or a direct video link.
- issue: No clips or highlights in the result | steps:; - The result shows No video clips generated. Try re-running. or No highlights extracted.; - Click Back to History and click Generate again.; - Try a different video or a different Max Highlights value.
commonProblems:

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Problems and limits.
- problem: An alert says Please upload a video or paste a video URL first. when I click Generate | whyItHappens: No source video is set. | howToFix: Upload a video, choose one under Saved, or paste an http:// or https:// video link, then click Generate again.
- problem: My file will not upload | whyItHappens: The file is over 100 MB, or is not recognised as a video. | howToFix: Compress or trim the video to under 100 MB and try again, or paste a link to a hosted copy.
- problem: Typing in the text box does nothing to my clips | whyItHappens: The text box text is not sent to the clipping service; only a pasted link is used. | howToFix: Use the aspect ratio, Max Highlights and Coordinates Only settings to steer the result.
- problem: Clicking a clip card does not open a bigger player | whyItHappens: Clip cards play a muted preview on hover. | howToFix: Hover over the card to preview it, or use Download to watch the full file.
- problem: The timeline shows entries called Highlight #1, Highlight #2 with 15-second steps | whyItHappens: If Coordinates Only returns no coordinates, the studio fills in placeholder entries (Highlight #n, each 15 seconds long, one after another). | howToFix: Treat those times as placeholders and run again, or switch Coordinates Only off to get rendered clips.
limitations:
- Uploaded video files are limited to 100 MB
- Generation needs your own MuAPI key

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Problems and limits.
- The bottom text box does not steer the clips

limitationDetails:
- limitation: Uploaded video files are limited to 100 MB | impact: Larger files are rejected with a size message before upload. | workaround: Trim or compress the video, or paste a link to a hosted copy.
- limitation: Generation needs your own MuAPI key | impact: Without a valid key generation is blocked. | workaround: Open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
- limitation: The bottom text box does not steer the clips | impact: Descriptions you type are not sent with the request. | workaround: Use aspect ratio, Max Highlights and Coordinates Only.
- limitation: History is local to this browser | impact: Past runs are saved in browser storage (up to 30) and do not follow you to another browser. | workaround: Download the clips you want to keep.
- limitation: Clip cards have no fullscreen player | impact: Clicking a card does not open a larger view. | workaround: Hover to preview or download the file.
faqs:
- question: Where do I open AI Clipping? | answer: Choose AI Clipping in the studio list, or go to /studio/clipping.
- question: How big can my video be? | answer: Files you upload can be up to 100 MB. Larger files are rejected with a message.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Problems and limits.
- question: Can I paste a link instead of uploading? | answer: Yes. Paste a link that starts with http:// or https:// into the bottom text box and it becomes the source video. Use a direct link to a video file.
- question: How many highlights can I ask for? | answer: From 1 to 60 using the Limit: slider in the Max Highlights menu. The default is 3.
- question: Which aspect ratios are available? | answer: 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3 and 3:4. The default is 9:16.
- question: What does Coordinates Only do? | answer: It asks for timing coordinates instead of rendered clips and shows them in a Highlights Timeline next to the Original Video Player. No clip files are returned in that mode.
- question: Does the text I type in the bottom box change the clips? | answer: No. Only the video link, highlight count, aspect ratio and Coordinates Only setting are sent.
- question: Where are my past runs? | answer: Click Back to History to see Clipping History Runs. They are saved in this browser only, up to 30 runs.
- question: How do I download a clip? | answer: Hover over the clip card and click Download (or use the actions menu on small screens). The file is saved as an .mp4.

chunks.title: AI Clipping — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI Clipping (/studio/clipping). Problems and limits.
- question: My generation failed. What should I check? | answer: Read the error message that appears at the bottom right. If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key. Then retry with a smaller video or a direct video link.

chunks.title: Vibe Motion — Overview
chunks.text:
Vibe Motion (/studio/vibe-motion). Overview.
description: Describe an animated motion graphic in words (kinetic typography, data charts, logo reveals) and get a rendered video; then remix a finished result by describing what to change.
shortDescription: Describe an animated motion graphic in words (kinetic typography, data charts, logo reveals) and get a rendered video; then remix a finished result by describing what to change.
fullDescription: Vibe Motion turns a text description into an animated motion graphic video. You write a prompt, choose an aspect ratio (16:9, 9:16 or 1:1) and a duration (5 to 30 seconds), and click Generate. Finished videos collect in a gallery in your browser. Each generation that returned an ID can be remixed: switch to Edit, pick the source generation, describe the change, and click Remix to produce a changed version. The loading screen notes that the graphic is rendered with React/Remotion on a remote service.
bestFor: Creators and marketers who need short animated graphics, titles and charts from a text prompt.
whenToUse:
- You want an animated chart, title or logo-style graphic from a text description
- You want to adjust an existing motion graphic by describing the change
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Video Studio for generated video scenes from text or images
- Use Motion Control Studio to copy motion from a reference video onto your character images

chunks.title: Vibe Motion — Overview
chunks.text:
Vibe Motion (/studio/vibe-motion). Overview.
- Use Cinema Studio for camera-directed footage
businessValue: Vibe Motion lets you get an animated graphic from a written description and iterate on it with remix, all in one screen.

chunks.title: Vibe Motion — How to use
chunks.text:
Vibe Motion (/studio/vibe-motion). How to use.
howToUse: Open Vibe Motion at /studio/vibe-motion, type a description of the motion graphic in the prompt box, optionally change the aspect ratio and duration buttons, then click Generate. To change a finished result, hover its card and click the remix button (tooltip Remix this generation), describe the change, and click Remix.
howToSteps:
- Open Vibe Motion: choose Vibe Motion in the studio list, or go to /studio/vibe-motion.
- Make sure the Generate option is selected at the top of the bottom bar (it is the default).
- Click the prompt box and describe the motion graphic, for example an animated sales dashboard with glowing bar charts and rising numbers.
- Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 16:9 at first) and choose 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1 from the Aspect Ratio menu.
- Click the duration button (it shows 6s at first) and choose a length from 5s up to 30s in the Duration menu.
- Click Generate (or press Ctrl+Enter). The button changes to Generating... and a Generating motion graphics… screen shows a running timer.
- When it finishes, the result appears as a card in the gallery. Hover over it to preview, or click it to watch it fullscreen.
- To save the video, hover the card and click the download button (tooltip Download).

chunks.title: Vibe Motion — How to use
chunks.text:
Vibe Motion (/studio/vibe-motion). How to use.
- To change a result: hover its card and click the remix button (tooltip Remix this generation), or click Edit and pick it under Pick source…. Describe what to change in the prompt box and click Remix (it shows Remixing... while it works). The new version is added to the gallery with an Edit tag.
- To leave Edit mode without remixing, click the x on the banner (tooltip Cancel Edit Mode) or click Generate in the toggle.
gettingStarted:
- Open Vibe Motion from the studio list (/studio/vibe-motion).
- Type a description of the motion graphic you want in the prompt box.
- Leave the defaults (16:9, 6s) for a first test, or change them with the two buttons next to the prompt.
- Click Generate and wait for the Generating motion graphics… screen to finish.
- Preview the card in the gallery, then Download it if you like it.
- Use the remix button on the card (Remix this generation) to try a variation.
tips:
- Be concrete: name the elements, colours, background and movement you want in the prompt.
- For a remix, describe only the change, for example the background colour or an added element.
- Pick 9:16 for vertical video and 1:1 for square before you generate.
- Use a short duration (5s or 6s) for a first test.
- Download results you want to keep: the gallery is stored in this browser only.
bestPractices:
- Describe subject, motion and style in one clear sentence or two.

chunks.title: Vibe Motion — How to use
chunks.text:
Vibe Motion (/studio/vibe-motion). How to use.
- Generate a first version, then use Edit to refine instead of rewriting the whole prompt.
- Match aspect ratio to the platform before generating.
- Compare versions in the gallery and delete the ones you do not need.

chunks.text:

chunks.title: Lip Sync — Overview
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). Overview.
description: Makes a talking video by syncing an audio track to a portrait image or to an existing video, with a choice of lip-sync and avatar models for each of the two input modes.
shortDescription: Turn a portrait image or an existing video, plus an audio file, into a lip-synced talking video.
fullDescription: Lip Sync Studio (the "Lip Sync" tab) has two input modes, "Portrait Image" and "Video". In Portrait Image mode you upload a still face image and an audio file and a model animates the face to speak that audio; the model list for this mode includes Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2 Speech to Video, LTX lipsync models, Kling avatar models and Omnihuman. In Video mode you upload an existing video and an audio file and a model re-syncs the speaker's mouth to the new audio; the list for this mode includes Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify, Veed, Infinite Talk V2V and a Volcengine model. You pick a model from a dropdown, optionally pick a resolution (only shown for models that offer one) and optionally type a short note in the text box (only sent to models that accept a prompt). Click "Sync Lip" and the finished video appears at the top of the gallery on the same page, where you can play it, open it full screen, download it, post it to social or delete it.
bestFor: Anyone who needs a speaking face from an image or a re-synced video, without filming.
whenToUse:

chunks.title: Lip Sync — Overview
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). Overview.
- You have a still image and a voice recording and want a talking video
- You have footage and want to change what the speaker says
- You want an avatar-style narrator from an image
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Audio Studio to create or clone the voice first
- Use Video Studio for general video generation from text or images
- Use Marketing Studio for product ads with avatars
businessValue: Produces speaking-face videos from a picture or existing footage plus an audio file, so you can create or re-voice clips without a new shoot.

chunks.title: Lip Sync — How to use
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). How to use.
howToUse: 1. Open Lip Sync Studio at /studio/lipsync (the "Lip Sync" tab in the studio tab bar). The bar at the bottom of the page holds all the controls. 2. Choose the input mode with the two buttons at the top of the bottom bar: "Portrait Image" (a still face plus audio) or "Video" (an existing video plus audio). "Portrait Image" is selected when you first open the studio. 3. Add your picture or video: click the round upload button (it opens a file picker), or drag a file onto it, or click "Library" and pick a saved file. Images must be under 10MB and videos under 50MB. The upload accepts JPG, PNG and WEBP images and MP4, WEBM and MOV videos. 4. Add your audio: click the microphone button (or drag an audio file onto it, or choose one from "Library"). Audio must be under 10MB; the upload accepts MP3, WAV and WEBM audio. Once uploaded, click the audio button to play or pause it, and click the small x on its corner to remove it. 5. Click the model button (it shows the current model name, or "Select model") and choose a model from the "Model" list. Switching mode resets the model to the first model of that mode. 6. If a resolution button appears next to the model button, click it and choose a size from the "Resolution" list. Models without a resolution choice do not show this button. 7. Optionally type a note in the text box (placeholder "Describe speech style..."). It is only used by models that accept a prompt; other models ignore it. 8. Click "Sync Lip". The button changes to "Generating..." until the video is ready. 9. When it finishes, the new video appears at the top of the gallery above the bar. Hover over it to preview, click it to open it full screen, and use the icons that appear on hover to copy the prompt, download it ("Download"), post it to social or delete it ("Delete").

chunks.title: Lip Sync — How to use
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). How to use.
howToSteps:
- Open Lip Sync Studio at /studio/lipsync (the "Lip Sync" tab in the studio tab bar). The bar at the bottom of the page holds all the controls.
- Choose the input mode with the two buttons at the top of the bottom bar: "Portrait Image" (a still face plus audio) or "Video" (an existing video plus audio). "Portrait Image" is selected when you first open the studio.
- Add your picture or video: click the round upload button (it opens a file picker), or drag a file onto it, or click "Library" and pick a saved file. Images must be under 10MB and videos under 50MB. The upload accepts JPG, PNG and WEBP images and MP4, WEBM and MOV videos.
- Add your audio: click the microphone button (or drag an audio file onto it, or choose one from "Library"). Audio must be under 10MB; the upload accepts MP3, WAV and WEBM audio. Once uploaded, click the audio button to play or pause it, and click the small x on its corner to remove it.
- Click the model button (it shows the current model name, or "Select model") and choose a model from the "Model" list. Switching mode resets the model to the first model of that mode.
- If a resolution button appears next to the model button, click it and choose a size from the "Resolution" list. Models without a resolution choice do not show this button.

chunks.title: Lip Sync — How to use
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). How to use.
- Optionally type a note in the text box (placeholder "Describe speech style..."). It is only used by models that accept a prompt; other models ignore it.
- Click "Sync Lip". The button changes to "Generating..." until the video is ready.
- When it finishes, the new video appears at the top of the gallery above the bar. Hover over it to preview, click it to open it full screen, and use the icons that appear on hover to copy the prompt, download it ("Download"), post it to social or delete it ("Delete").
gettingStarted:
- Open Lip Sync Studio from the studio tab bar ("Lip Sync") or go to /studio/lipsync.
- Pick "Portrait Image" if you have a still face, or "Video" if you want to change the speech in existing footage.
- Upload your image or video, then upload your audio with the microphone button.
- Choose a model (and a resolution if that button is shown).
- Click "Sync Lip" and wait for the video to appear at the top of the gallery.
- Download it, post it to social, or keep generating variations with a different model.
tips:
- Start with a short audio clip and the default model to check the result before running longer audio or a different model.
- Use a clear, front-facing portrait with the whole face visible in Portrait Image mode.
- Use clean audio with little background noise so the mouth movement follows the speech clearly.

chunks.title: Lip Sync — How to use
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). How to use.
- Resolution and model are independent: if a model offers 480p, 720p or 1080p, the default is shown on the button, so check it before you generate.
- Your uploads, selected model, resolution, text and recent results are remembered in your browser between visits, so you can leave and come back.
- Use the text box only with models that accept a prompt; it has no effect on the video-to-video models such as Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify, Veed or Volcengine.
bestPractices:
- Convert audio to MP3 or WAV before uploading, because the upload rejects other audio types.
- Keep images under 10MB, videos under 50MB and audio under 10MB; the studio refuses larger files before uploading.
- Use Video mode when you already have footage of the speaker and only want to change the spoken audio; use Portrait Image mode when you only have a still image.
- Compare two models on the same short clip before committing to a long one.
- Download results you want to keep; the gallery lists only your 30 most recent results.

- question: What is the difference between Portrait Image and Video mode? | answer: Portrait Image mode animates a still face image so it speaks your audio. Video mode takes an existing video and re-syncs the speaker's mouth to your audio.
- question: What file types and sizes can I upload? | answer: Images up to 10MB (JPG, PNG, WEBP), videos up to 50MB (MP4, WEBM, MOV) and audio up to 10MB (MP3, WAV, WEBM). Larger or other types are refused.

chunks.title: Lip Sync — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). Problems and limits.
- question: Why is there no Resolution button? | answer: The Resolution button only appears for models that offer a resolution choice. Choose a different model if you need one.
- question: Does the text box change the result? | answer: Only for models that accept a prompt. The video-to-video lip-sync models ignore it.
- question: Where does my finished video go? | answer: To the top of the gallery on the same page. It stays in your browser; the gallery keeps the 30 most recent results, so download anything you want to keep.
- question: Can I reuse a file I uploaded earlier? | answer: Yes. Click "Library" and pick it from the tabs. In Portrait Image mode the tabs are Images and Audio; in Video mode they are Videos and Audio.
- question: How do I remove an uploaded file? | answer: Click the small x on the corner of the upload button. For image and video, clicking the button itself also clears it; for audio, clicking the button plays or pauses it.
- question: Can I drag and drop files? | answer: Yes. Drop a file onto the matching upload button. Files dropped onto the studio are also picked up: audio fills the audio slot, a video switches to Video mode and an image switches to Portrait Image mode.

chunks.title: Lip Sync — Problems and limits

Lip Sync (/studio/lipsync). Problems and limits.
- question: How do I download a result? | answer: Hover over the result card in the gallery and click the Download icon (tooltip "Download"). On small screens use the actions menu on the card.
- question: Why do I see a message about my MuAPI key? | answer: If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). Overview.
description: Generates cinematic still images from a text description, with a camera body, lens, focal length and aperture that you choose in a Camera settings panel.
shortDescription: Describe a scene, choose a camera, lens, focal length and aperture, and shoot a cinematic still image.
fullDescription: Cinema Studio produces still images, not video. You type a scene description, optionally add one reference image, pick an aspect ratio and a resolution (1K, 2K or 4K), and open the camera summary button to choose a camera body, a lens, a focal length and an aperture in the "Camera settings" panel. When you click "Shoot", the studio adds your camera choices and some fixed quality wording to your text and generates the image. With a reference image attached it edits or builds on that image; without one it generates from text alone. Results are added to a gallery on the same page, where you can open them full screen, copy the prompt or the image, download, post to social or delete them.
bestFor: Creators who want film-style stills and key art with camera-style controls.
whenToUse:
- You want a cinematic-looking still from text
- You want to control camera, lens, focal length and aperture
- You want to rework one existing image
whenToUseAnother:
- Use Video Studio for motion
- Use Image Studio to choose a specific image model or use several reference images

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). Overview.
- Use Storyboard to plan a sequence of shots
businessValue: Produces film-style still images from text, with camera-style choices handled for you.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). How to use.
howToUse: 1. Open Cinema Studio at /studio/cinema (the "Cinema Studio" tab in the studio tab bar). The controls are in the bar at the bottom of the page. 2. Type your scene in the text box (placeholder "Describe your cinema scene..."). The "Shoot" button stays disabled until the box has text. 3. Optional: add a reference image. Click the round picture button at the left of the text box to choose a file, drag an image onto it, or click "Library" to reuse a saved image. Click the picture again (an x appears on hover) to remove it. 4. Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 16:9 at first) and choose from the "Aspect Ratio" list: 16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5. 5. Click the resolution button (it shows 2K at first) and choose from the "Resolution" list: 1K, 2K or 4K. 6. Click the camera summary button at the right of the controls (it reads like "Modular 8K Digital · Creative Tilt Lens, 35mm, f/1.4"). The "Camera settings" panel opens. 7. In the panel, scroll or drag each of the four columns, "Camera", "Lens", "Focal length" and "Aperture", until the option you want sits in the highlighted middle row; clicking an option also scrolls it into place. Close the panel with the Close button at the top right, with the Escape key, or by clicking outside it. 8. Click "Shoot". The button shows "Generating..." while the image is made. 9. The new image appears at the top of the gallery. Click it to open it full screen. Hover over a card to show the action icons: copy prompt, copy image, "Download", Post to social, an AI assist star and "Delete".

- Optional: add a reference image. Click the round picture button at the left of the text box to choose a file, drag an image onto it, or click "Library" to reuse a saved image. Click the picture again (an x appears on hover) to remove it.
- Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 16:9 at first) and choose from the "Aspect Ratio" list: 16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5.
- Click the resolution button (it shows 2K at first) and choose from the "Resolution" list: 1K, 2K or 4K.

Close the panel with the Close button at the top right, with the Escape key, or by clicking outside it.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (/studio/cinema). How to use.
- The new image appears at the top of the gallery. Click it to open it full screen. Hover over a card to show the action icons: copy prompt, copy image, "Download", Post to social, an AI assist star and "Delete".
gettingStarted:
- Open Cinema Studio from the studio tab bar or go to /studio/cinema.
- Type a scene description into the box that says "Describe your cinema scene...".
- Open the camera summary button and choose a camera, lens, focal length and aperture, then close the panel.
- Choose an aspect ratio and a resolution.
- Click "Shoot" and wait for the image to appear in the gallery.
- Hover over the image to download it or copy its prompt.
tips:
- Describe subject, setting and mood in your own words; the camera, lens, focal length and aperture you pick are added for you, so you do not need to type them.
- Pick the aspect ratio before shooting: 21:9 for wide cinematic frames, 9:16 for vertical video covers, 1:1 or 4:5 for social posts.
- Use f/1.4 for a shallow depth of field and f/11 for a sharp background; the panel shows the choices as a scrolling list.
- Try 1K or 2K while you are experimenting and 4K when you are happy with the framing.
- Settings, text, the reference image and your recent shots are remembered in your browser between visits.
- Use "Copy prompt" on a gallery card to reuse the text of a shot you liked.

chunks.title: Storyboard — Overview
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). Overview.
description: Plan a short film as scenes with camera settings and characters, draw a still frame for each scene, export the board as JSON, PDF or an animated GIF, or render it as one storyboard video.
shortDescription: Plan a short film as scenes with camera settings and characters, draw a still frame for each scene, export the board as JSON, PDF or an animated GIF, or render it as one storyboard video.
fullDescription: Storyboard is a planning studio. You write a project name and a creative brief, split the brief into scenes, give each scene a length and optional camera settings, tag the characters that appear in it, and draw a still frame for each scene. You can then export the board (JSON, PDF, or an animated GIF of the frames), generate one storyboard video from all the scenes with the Generate Storyboard button, or send the board to Video Studio, Cinema Studio or VFX Studio. Scene frames can be drawn by a MuAPI image model or by OpenAI image models (using your own OpenAI key from Settings); the OpenAI option also lets you edit a frame with a text instruction and guide the layout with a rough sketch. Your projects are kept in this browser.
bestFor: Creators, marketers and directors who want to plan a video visually before generating it.
whenToUse:
- Planning a short film or ad scene by scene
- Showing frames and camera ideas to a client

Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). How to use.
howToUse: Open Storyboard from the studio list (route /studio/storyboard). On the Storyboard page type a PROJECT NAME and CREATIVE BRIEF, pick the ASPECT RATIO and CLIP LENGTH, add scenes (Quick-add a scene or Brief → scenes), optionally add Characters, then open Shot Editor to set camera options and draw a still frame for each scene. Back on the Storyboard page use Generate Storyboard to make the storyboard video, or export with JSON, PDF or Send to.
howToSteps:
- Open Storyboard from the studio list. The Storyboard page opens with a PROJECT bar at the top; click New to start a fresh project, or choose an existing one in the project drop-down.
- In 1. Project & Creative Brief, type a PROJECT NAME (the placeholder reads My Animated Series) and describe the story in CREATIVE BRIEF, one line per scene works best.
- Choose the ASPECT RATIO (16:9 or 9:16) and the CLIP LENGTH (5s or 10s).
- Click Brief → scenes to create one scene for each line (or each sentence, if the brief is a single paragraph). You can also type a scene into Quick-add a scene… and click Add. Each scene starts with a length; the page shows the total against the clip length and a Fit to button if they do not match.
- Optional: in the Characters box, enter a Name, Traits and a reference image (use Upload or paste a URL), then click Add Character. Characters are tagged onto scenes later.

chunks.title: Storyboard — How to use
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). How to use.
- Click Shot Editor. For each scene you can edit the text, set its length in seconds, tag characters, and open Camera to choose SHOT TYPE, ANGLE, MOVEMENT, CAMERA, LENS, FOCAL and APERTURE (each one can stay on Any).
- In Shot Editor choose the FRAME ENGINE: MuAPI (pick the image model with the model button at the top right) or OpenAI Images (pick the OpenAI image model and Panel detail).
- Click Frame on a scene to draw its still frame. The button changes to Regenerate once a frame exists. With OpenAI Images you can also add a Sketch before generating, and use the Change this frame box with Edit after a frame exists.
- Drag the handle on a scene card to reorder scenes.
- To save the board, go back to the Storyboard page and use JSON or PDF at the top right. To make an animated preview, set seconds per frame in the ANIMATED GIF row of Shot Editor and click Export GIF.
- To render a video from all scenes, click Generate Storyboard in 3. Generate Storyboard Video and wait for the player to appear. Use Send to to continue in Video Studio, Cinema Studio or VFX Studio.
gettingStarted:
- Open Storyboard from the studio list (it opens on the Storyboard page).
- Type a PROJECT NAME and a CREATIVE BRIEF with one line per scene.
- Pick ASPECT RATIO and CLIP LENGTH, then click Brief → scenes.
- Open Shot Editor and click Frame on a scene to see your first still frame.

chunks.title: Storyboard — How to use
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). How to use.
- Come back to the Storyboard page and click Generate Storyboard when the scenes are ready.
tips:
- Write the brief one line per scene; Brief → scenes then gives you a ready scene list.
- Keep the scene lengths close to the clip length. If the total is off, the page shows a warning and a Fit to button that rescales every scene.
- Add a reference image to each character; it is sent with every scene where that character is tagged so the character stays recognisable.
- Use OpenAI Images when you want to refine one frame: type what to change in the Change this frame box and click Edit.
- Choose a low Panel detail (Low detail (fastest)) while testing ideas and a higher one for final frames.
- Export GIF needs at least one generated frame; only scenes that already have a frame are included.
bestPractices:
- Plan the story first (brief and scenes), then add characters, then draw frames; frames use the scene text, tagged characters and camera settings.
- Use one aspect ratio per project. The aspect ratio you choose on the Storyboard page is used for frames, the GIF and the video.
- Draw frames one scene at a time and use Regenerate until you are happy, then export.
- Use the PROJECT switcher to keep separate stories apart; each project keeps its own scenes and characters.

keyFeatures:

chunks.title: Storyboard — Features
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). Features.
modelCapabilities: Frames can be drawn by a MuAPI image model (picked with the model button in Shot Editor, which opens a list with a Search models... box and provider filter) or, when FRAME ENGINE is OpenAI Images, by an OpenAI image model chosen in the OpenAI image model drop-down. The storyboard video is generated by the storyboard video service from the scene list, clip length, aspect ratio and (if present) the first character reference image.
modelExplanations: Two engines draw scene frames. MuAPI uses the model chosen with the model button at the top right of Shot Editor and sends the reference images of tagged characters along. OpenAI Images uses an OpenAI image model chosen in the OpenAI image model drop-down plus a Panel detail setting (Low detail (fastest), Medium detail, High detail); it also supports Edit and Sketch. The on-screen hint says the faster option is for trying ideas and the more detailed one is better for busy scenes. The storyboard video uses its own service and only accepts a 5 or 10 second clip.

chunks.title: Storyboard — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Storyboard (/studio/storyboard). Problems and limits.
troubleshooting:
- Generate Storyboard does nothing or shows a plan message: Make sure there is at least one scene with text.
- Frame generation fails: Confirm the scene has text; the Frame button is disabled for an empty scene.
- Sketch button is missing: Sketch and Edit only appear when FRAME ENGINE is set to OpenAI Images.
- Export GIF is disabled: Generate at least one frame first; the button title says 'Generate at least one frame first'.
- The PDF does not appear: Allow pop-ups for the site; if they are blocked an HTML file is downloaded instead.
- Cannot switch project or leave the page: The project bar and the Shot Editor and Analysis buttons are locked while a storyboard video is generating; wait for it to finish.
troubleshootingSteps:
- issue: Generate Storyboard does nothing or shows a plan message | steps:; - Make sure there is at least one scene with text.; - If you see 'An active plan is required to generate storyboards.', check that your plan is active.; - If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

chunks.text:

- issue: Sketch button is missing | steps:; - Sketch and Edit only appear when FRAME ENGINE is set to OpenAI Images.; - The Change this frame box also needs a generated frame.
- issue: Export GIF is disabled | steps:; - Generate at least one frame first; the button title says 'Generate at least one frame first'.
